families.summary: Engineering majors start with calculus, physics and chemistry in the first college year, so plan to reach calculus by 12th grade and take math every year.

math.note: Take math every year. Precalculus plus a test score or placement exam is the minimum that keeps the path open.

gates.text: UT Austin requires calculus readiness to apply to every engineering major: a qualifying SAT, ACT, CLT, AP or IB score, or Calculus I with a B or higher, received by December 10 of 12th grade.
UT Knoxville engineering looks for a Success Prediction Indicator of at least 60 and an ACT math score of 25 or SAT math score of 590; students below that are reviewed holistically.
Texas A&M encourages engineering applicants to take a math class higher than precalculus.
The University of Utah expects engineering students to finish calculus in their first year; starting college ready for Calculus I helps, though it isn't required.

families.summary: Engineering technology and drafting programs apply math and physics to hands-on work. Bachelor's programs use calculus or math above trigonometry; associate programs use algebra and trigonometry.

math.note: For an associate program, Algebra II with trigonometry is the target.

families.summary: Computer science and data science majors lean on calculus, discrete math and programming. Plan to reach calculus by 12th grade and take computer science along the way.

math.note: Discrete math helps if your school offers it.

gates.text: UT Austin requires calculus readiness to apply to computer science and its joint majors: a qualifying SAT, ACT, CLT, AP or IB score, or Calculus I with a B or higher, received by December 10 of 12th grade.

For 2027 terms, the University of Houston's College of Natural Sciences & Mathematics asks for precalculus, Algebra I and II, Geometry, 4 English and 2 of biology, chemistry or physics for automatic admission.

cautions.text: UT Austin counts computer science as a foreign language for its admission prerequisites.

families.summary: IT, networking and cybersecurity careers can start with certifications or an associate degree. Algebra II plus a 4th math works; aim for calculus if you might study computer science or engineering.

math.note: Calculus if you're aiming for a computer science or engineering bachelor's degree.

cautions.text: Some IT support jobs start with a high school diploma plus IT certifications.

families.summary: Math, statistics, chemistry, physics and earth science majors use calculus from the first year. Take the highest math your school offers, plus chemistry and physics.

gates.text: UT Austin requires calculus readiness for all geosciences majors (a qualifying test score, or Calculus I with a B or higher, received by December 10 of 12th grade).

For 2027 terms, the University of Houston's College of Natural Sciences & Mathematics asks for precalculus, Algebra I and II, Geometry, 4 English and 2 of biology, chemistry or physics for automatic admission.

families.summary: Biology majors take chemistry and biology from the start, often with calculus or statistics. Calculus by 12th grade is the target; precalculus keeps the path open.

gates.text: UT Austin requires calculus readiness for its Environmental Science (Biological Sciences) major.

For 2027 terms, the University of Houston's College of Natural Sciences & Mathematics asks for precalculus, Algebra I and II, Geometry, 4 English and 2 of biology, chemistry or physics for automatic admission.

families.summary: Medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, physical therapy and veterinary medicine are graduate or professional degrees. Plan for the college major first (often biology) with strong biology, chemistry and physics.

gates.text: For 2027 terms, the University of Houston's College of Natural Sciences & Mathematics asks for precalculus, Algebra I and II, Geometry, 4 English and 2 of biology, chemistry or physics for automatic admission.

cautions.text: Professional programs set their own prerequisites, like anatomy, chemistry and physics for physical therapy. A few programs admit students straight from high school.
Veterinary colleges look for many science classes, including biology, chemistry and animal science.

families.summary: Registered nursing programs start with biology, chemistry, anatomy and statistics. Algebra II plus statistics is the math target.

gates.text: UT Knoxville's freshman direct admission to nursing is highly competitive. Students expecting more than 45 dual enrollment hours, or an associate degree, by graduation should contact the College of Nursing before applying.
UT Austin admits nursing students directly as freshmen; the deadline is December 1.
For 2027 terms, the University of Houston's nursing college asks for biology, two more sciences, algebra, geometry, one more math and 3 English credits for automatic admission.

cautions.text: In Texas, finishing the Nursing Science program of study meets the STEM endorsement's program requirement if the STEM math and science requirements are met; otherwise it counts toward Public Services.

families.summary: Practical nursing (LPN or LVN) and nurse aide (CNA) training can start in high school career and technical programs. Algebra II plus a 4th math, like medical math, is the target.

math.note: Medical math is a good 4th math if your school offers it.

cautions.text: Nursing assistants usually finish a state-approved program and pass a state exam. Practical nursing programs take about a year and are offered at some high schools. Age and hour rules vary by state; ask your counselor.

families.summary: Allied health careers (imaging, respiratory care, dental hygiene, lab science, medical assisting) build on biology and chemistry, with physics for imaging and respiratory care.

math.note: Precalculus or statistics for bachelor's-degree programs.

cautions.text: For radiology or MRI technology, take anatomy, biology, chemistry and physics.
Medical assistants benefit from biology and chemistry.

families.summary: Kinesiology, athletic training, public health and nutrition majors build on biology, chemistry and anatomy, with precalculus and statistics.
Agriculture, animal and plant science programs build on chemistry and biology. Science tracks aim for precalculus; agribusiness and ag education can aim for Algebra II plus statistics.
Natural resources and environmental science combine biology, chemistry, earth science and math. Some programs require calculus; otherwise precalculus plus statistics works.

math.note: Calculus where the program requires it.

gates.text: UT Austin requires calculus readiness to apply to both environmental science majors: a qualifying SAT, ACT, CLT, AP or IB score, or Calculus I with a B or higher, received by December 10 of 12th grade.

families.summary: Architecture and interior design combine math, physics and art. Plan for calculus and physics, plus drawing or studio art.

gates.text: UT Austin's School of Architecture makes portfolios optional for freshman applicants.
UT Knoxville's College of Architecture and Design looks at grades, personal narratives and test scores, and in some cases a portfolio.

cautions.text: Most architects earn a 5-year Bachelor of Architecture.

families.summary: Business, accounting and finance majors use math, economics and communication. Calculus helps for selective business schools; otherwise precalculus or statistics.

math.note: Calculus for selective direct-admission business schools; otherwise precalculus or statistics.

gates.text: At the University of Utah, business students reach the upper division first and then apply separately to each business major.

families.summary: Economics majors use calculus and statistics. Keep taking math through high school and take an economics class if your school offers one.
Psychology majors take statistics early, and biology matters for science tracks. Algebra II plus statistics is the math target.
Government, history, sociology and pre-law build on strong writing, history, government and a world language. Statistics is useful for social science research.

cautions.text: Most law schools don't require a specific college major.

families.summary: Communication, journalism and media majors build on four years of English with writing, plus journalism, yearbook or speech.
English, world languages and humanities majors build on four years of English and as much of one world language as your school offers.

cautions.text: Selective colleges often suggest at least three years of the same language.

families.summary: Teaching and early childhood careers start with a teaching pathway if your school has one. Future math or science teachers should follow that subject's family.

math.note: Future math or science teachers follow that subject's math target.

cautions.text: Preschool teachers typically need at least an associate degree.

families.summary: Social work and human services majors take psychology, sociology and statistics, plus biology.
Visual arts, design, photography and animation programs look at your work. Take art every year, draw from observation, and build a portfolio.

gates.text: UT Austin's Studio Art program asks for a portfolio of 12 to 15 works, with 2 made from direct observation.

cautions.text: Some art schools ask for sketches and other examples of your work when you apply.

families.summary: Music programs usually hold auditions. Play or sing in an ensemble every year, study your instrument or voice, and take music theory if you can.
Theatre, dance and film programs often have their own application, audition or portfolio. Take theatre or dance classes and join productions.

gates.text: UT Austin Theatre and Dance applicants also apply to the department: the university deadline is December 1 and department materials are due December 10.

families.summary: Law enforcement, fire and EMS careers build on life sciences and anatomy, plus a career and technical pathway if your school has one.

cautions.text: Future EMTs should take life science classes and consider CPR certification. Age rules for EMT certification vary by state; ask your counselor.

families.summary: Electricians, plumbers, HVAC technicians and carpenters learn through apprenticeships and licenses. Algebra I, Geometry and Algebra II with applied math, plus physics for HVAC.

cautions.text: Licensing varies by state; plumbers often need 2 to 5 years of experience and an exam to work on their own.

families.summary: Welding and machining careers use geometry, shop math, blueprint reading and CAD. A career and technical pathway plus a credential is the core.

math.note: Geometry and shop math matter most.

cautions.text: Employers often prefer or require a high school diploma plus technical training.

families.summary: Automotive, diesel and aircraft maintenance careers use math, electronics and computers. A career and technical pathway plus a credential is the core.

cautions.text: An FAA mechanic certificate requires being at least 18, so you can train in high school and certify later.

families.summary: Pilot careers use physics and precalculus, and airline pilots typically need a bachelor's degree and flight experience.

cautions.text: FAA minimum ages: 16 for a student pilot (14 for a glider or balloon), 17 for a private pilot, 18 for a commercial pilot, and 23 for an airline transport pilot (21 in some cases).
Airline pilots typically need a bachelor's degree and experience as a commercial or military pilot.

families.summary: Culinary and hospitality careers build on a culinary or hospitality pathway and food-safety credentials. Business or financial math fits well.

math.note: Business or financial math is a good 4th math.

cautions.text: Some states and localities require a food handler's certification.

families.summary: Cosmetology and barbering careers need a state-approved program and a license exam. A career and technical pathway can start that in high school.

cautions.text: A license usually means finishing a state-approved program and passing an exam. Hours, age and other rules vary by state; ask your counselor.
